questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: What is the solution of the equation 3x + 7 = 22?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: 3x = 15, then divide by 3: x = 5.
questions.hint: Isolate the term with x first.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of the following values are roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: x² − 5x + 6 factorises as (x − 2)(x − 3), so the roots are 2 and 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Differentiate f(x) = x³ · sin(x). Show your working and give f'(x) on the last line.
questions.model_answer: Product rule: f'(x) = (x³)' sin x + x³ (sin x)' = 3x² sin x + x³ cos x

criteria.description: Recognises and applies the product rule
Correct derivatives of x³ and sin(x)

questions.explanation: Use the product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv' with u = x³ and v = sin x.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate the definite integral of 2x from x = 1 to x = 4.
questions.explanation: An antiderivative of 2x is x², so the integral is 4² − 1² = 16 − 1 = 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The probability of getting two heads when tossing two fair coins is 1/4.
questions.explanation: The outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT are equally likely; only HH has two heads, so P = 1/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is ___ degrees, and of a quadrilateral it is ___ degrees.
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A ladder 5 m long leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is 1.4 m from the wall. At what height (in metres) does the ladder touch the wall? Give the answer with a unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 8 s. What distance does it cover in that time? Include the unit.
questions.explanation: Distance = average velocity × time = (0 + 20)/2 × 8 = 80 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which quantity is a vector?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others are scalars.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A resistor of 12 Ω carries a current of 0.5 A. What is the voltage across it? Include the unit.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: U = R·I = 12 Ω × 0.5 A = 6 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: What is the name of the temperature at which all molecular motion would be minimal and which equals 0 K?
questions.explanation: 0 K is absolute zero (−273.15 °C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Explain Newton's third law of motion and why the two forces in an action–reaction pair do not cancel each other out. Give an everyday example.

criteria.description: States the law correctly: forces come in equal and opposite pairs
Explains that the forces act on different bodies and therefore do not cancel
Gives a correct everyday example and identifies both forces

common_misconceptions: The forces cancel because they are equal and opposite
The larger object exerts a larger force

questions.model_answer: For every force that body A exerts on body B, B exerts a force of equal magnitude and opposite direction on A. The pair does not cancel because the two forces act on different bodies; cancellation only applies to forces acting on the same body. Example: when walking, your foot pushes the ground backwards and the ground pushes you forwards.
questions.explanation: Action–reaction forces act on different objects, so each object's motion is determined by the forces on it alone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the molar mass of water (H2O) in g/mol? Use H = 1.008 and O = 16.00.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A solution has pH 3. How would you describe it?
questions.explanation: pH below 7 is acidic at 25 °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match each subatomic particle with its electric charge.
questions.explanation: Protons are positive, electrons negative, neutrons neutral.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Which organelle is the main site of aerobic ATP production in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria produces most of the cell's ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Put the stages of protein synthesis in the correct order.
order_items: mRNA is processed and leaves the nucleus
tRNA brings amino acids according to codons
questions.explanation: Transcription in the nucleus precedes translation on ribosomes, where tRNAs deliver amino acids until a stop codon.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.text: Two heterozygous pea plants (Aa × Aa) are crossed. What percentage of the offspring are expected to show the recessive phenotype?
questions.explanation: Punnett square: AA, Aa, Aa, aa → 1/4 = 25 % are aa.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the search interval, so at most ⌈log₂ n⌉ + 1 comparisons are needed.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Match each data structure with the access pattern it is best known for.

match_pairs.right: Fast access to the minimum or maximum

questions.explanation: These are the defining operations of each structure.

questions.text: Write a Python function is_palindrome(s) that returns True if the string s reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and spaces, and False otherwise.
questions.explanation: Normalise the string (remove spaces, lower-case) and compare it with its reverse.

questions.subject: Programming
questions.text: What is the name of the condition that stops a recursive function from calling itself forever?
questions.explanation: Every recursive function needs a base case that returns without a further recursive call.

questions.subject: History
questions.text: In which year did the First World War begin?
questions.explanation: The war began in July 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

questions.subject: History
questions.text: Arrange these Cold War events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: Berlin Blockade (1948–49), Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), Prague Spring (1968), Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989).

questions.subject: History
questions.text: Case study: In 1929 the US stock market crashed. Over the following years industrial production fell sharply, unemployment rose to about a quarter of the workforce, and international trade contracted as many countries raised tariffs (for example the Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act of 1930). Banks failed in large numbers and deflation increased the real burden of debts. Task: Analyse two mechanisms through which the crash turned into a prolonged worldwide depression and evaluate one policy response.

criteria.description: Identifies a valid transmission mechanism (e.g. bank failures and credit contraction, deflation and debt burden, collapse of demand)
Identifies a second distinct mechanism, including the international dimension (tariffs, gold standard, capital flows)
Evaluates a policy response (e.g. New Deal, leaving the gold standard, protectionism) with reasoned judgement
Uses evidence from the case and stays relevant

questions.model_answer: Bank failures destroyed deposits and cut credit, reducing investment and consumption; deflation raised real debt burdens causing defaults. Internationally, protectionist tariffs like Smoot–Hawley triggered retaliation, collapsing trade, while the gold standard transmitted deflation between countries. Leaving the gold standard allowed monetary expansion and countries that left earlier recovered sooner, which suggests it was an effective response.
questions.explanation: Strong answers link financial, monetary and trade mechanisms and judge policies by evidence of recovery.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.text: Which of the following would shift the demand curve for coffee to the right? Select all that apply.

options.text: A rise in consumers' incomes (coffee is a normal good)
A fall in the price of coffee
A rise in the price of tea (a substitute)
A fall in the price of coffee beans for producers

questions.explanation: Income and the price of substitutes shift demand; coffee's own price moves along the curve; input costs shift supply.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: The Amazon River flows into the Pacific Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Amazon flows east and empties into the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.subject: Statistics
questions.text: What is the median of the data set 7, 3, 9, 1, 5, 11?
questions.explanation: Sorted: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. With an even count, the median is the mean of the middle values (5 + 7)/2 = 6.

questions.subject: Languages
questions.text: Complete the sentence with the correct past simple form: Yesterday she ___ (go) to the library and ___ (buy) a book.
questions.explanation: 'Go' and 'buy' are irregular verbs: go → went, buy → bought.
